rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to fear the Creator reinforces the opening command but adds creation of them and earlier peoples as proof that God deserves fear; the conjunction signals this added basis.
rows.anchor: وزاد فيه دليل استحقاقه التقوى بأن الله خلقهم وخلق الأمم من قبلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God the one who created them hints that they should abandon fearing or worshipping their associated partners.
rows.anchor: إيماء إلى نبذ اتقاء غيره من شركائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With kasra on jīm and bāʾ and a doubled lām, al-jibilla means creation or created beings; it is a noun like a verbal noun, hence its description as earlier.
rows.anchor: بكسر الجيم والباء وتشديد اللام : الخلقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative takes al-jibilla to mean the people possessing that nature: the earlier peoples.
rows.anchor: أطلق الجبلة على أهلها ، أي وذوي الجبلة الأولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They deny his prophethood by calling him bewitched, meaning magic has impaired his perception and ideas; this implicitly denies that his message comes from God.
rows.anchor: فزعموه مسحورا ، أي مختل الإدراك والتصورات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrasing min al-musahharin intensifies the accusation, as in similar expressions in the earlier stories of Noah, Salih, and Lot.
rows.anchor: من المبالغة ما تقدم في قوله : { من المرجومين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coordinating waw makes the claim that Shuayb is human a second argument against his prophethood; the Thamud account omits waw and treats humanity as evidence his speech is not revelation but an effect of bewitchment, though the conclusions converge.
rows.anchor: يجعل كونه بشرا إبطالا ثانيا لرسالته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ẓann means certainty, a common usage; the lām before its second object signals the original oath lām. Compare the same usage in 2:46.
rows.anchor: على المفعول الثاني ل ( ظن ) لأن أصلها لام قسم

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: Nafi, Ibn Amir, and Abu Jafar read the command with fāʾ, making trust in God follow from the disavowal in 26:216 and urging immediate refuge from the enemies.
rows.anchor: قراءة نافع وابن عامر وأبي جعفر فيكون تفريعا

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read with wāw, coordinating trust with the conditional answer; its connection to the condition likewise entails prompt action, so the readings yield the same result by different routes.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : { وتوكل } بالواو وهو عطف على جواب الشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the Prophet's close kin disobey him, he is to disavow their conduct; because this entails estrangement and enmity, God steadies him to rely on his Lord rather than fear them.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : فإن عصاك أهل عشيرتك فتبرأ منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is sufficient for the one who trusts Him, as stated in 65:3; this supports the command to rely on Him against hostile kin.
rows.anchor: ومن يتوكل على الله فهو حسبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The names al-Aziz and al-Rahim, the following relative clause, and the closing description signal that God attends to the Prophet's words and knows his intent; His might defeats stronger enemies and His mercy protects him.
rows.anchor: أنه يلاحظ قوله ويعلم نيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawakkul is entrusting one's affair to one who will suffice one's need; Ibn Ashur previously discussed it at 3:159.
rows.anchor: تفويض المرء أمره إلى من يكفيه مهمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description means God's special care: He sees the Prophet turning toward Him and accepts that devotion, like the expression in 52:48.
rows.anchor: رؤية خاصة وهي رؤية الإقبال والتقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's standing refers to prayer during the middle of the night, an established Quranic usage.
rows.anchor: غلب هذا الاسم عليه في اصطلاح القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His movement among those prostrating refers to his prayer with the Muslim congregation in his mosque.
rows.anchor: هو صلاته في جماعات المسلمين في مسجده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The compact pairing conveys care for Muslims alongside care for their Messenger, presenting that as part of his blessing.
rows.anchor: يجمع معنى العناية بالمسلمين تبعا للعناية برسولهم

rows.speaker: الزجاج والزمخشري وغيرهما
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj, al-Zamakhshari, and others take إذ as an object governed by an omitted اذكر and as a general time expression, not a temporal adverb, paralleling 2:30.
rows.anchor: الزجاج والزمخشري وغيرهما : انتصب { إذ } بفعل مضمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The new passage parallels the Prophet's receiving the Quran with Moses receiving God's speech when called, It is a deft transition from praise of revelation to prophetic stories.
rows.anchor: ومناسبة موقعها إفادة تنظير تلقي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم القرآن بتلقي موسى عليه السلام كلام الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story follows praise of the Quran as a transition to the next kind of Quranic inimitability: reporting unseen events, counted as the fourth aspect in the tenth introductory discussion.
rows.anchor: وذلك من بديع التخلص إلى ذكر قصص هؤلاء الأنبياء عقب التنويه بالقرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative that begins with Moses speaking to his family prepares for the call in 27:8; his remark came as he was about to receive revelation.
rows.anchor: تمهيد لجملة { فلما جاءها نودي أن بورك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story serves as a model for Muhammad and his people, embedding Moses's pre-mission circumstances in an admonition.
rows.anchor: فهذه القصة مثل ضربه الله لحال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مع قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ahl means Moses's wife: she was the addressee, and he had only her and two young sons with him; al-ahl is a euphemistic way to refer to a wife.
rows.anchor: مراد به زوجه ، ولم يكن معه إلا زوجه وابنان صغيران

rows.speaker: الحديث
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur cites the hadith wording والله ما علمت على أهلي إلا خيرا as usage of al-ahl for one's wife.
rows.anchor: والله ما علمت على أهلي إلا خيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire appeared only to Moses because it was an otherworldly light shown to him, not an ordinary fire; the emphatic إن suggests his wife doubted its appearance since she could not see it.
rows.anchor: ولم تظهر النار إلا لموسى دون غيره من أهله لأنها لم تكن نارا معتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-inas is sensing or noticing something subtle, whether seen or heard; al-Harith ibn Hilliza's line is cited for the verb آنست.
rows.anchor: الإحساس والشعور بأمر خفي ، فيكون في المرئيات وفي الأصوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The requested khabar is news about the place from which the fire appears.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالخبر خبر المكان الذي تلوح منه النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses may have hoped to find a household that would host them, or travelers with an ember to light roadside wood and warm the family.
rows.anchor: ولعله ظن أن هنالك بيتا يرجو استضافتهم إياه وأهله تلك الليلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A shihab is a burning ember; a qabas is an ember or flame taken from another fire to kindle wood or a wick.
rows.anchor: الجمر المشتعل . والقبس : جمرة أو شعلة نار تقبس

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read شهاب قبس as an annexation of a general term to a specific one, like خاتم حديد.
rows.anchor: قرأ الجمهور بإضافة { شهاب } إلى { قبس } إضافة العام إلى الخاص

rows.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي ويعقوب وخلف
rows.claim: Asim, Hamza, al-Kisai, Yaqoub, and Khalaf read شهاب with nunation; قبس is then either an appositive or an adjective.
rows.anchor: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي ويعقوب وخلف بتنوين { شهاب }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iṣṭilāʾ is an iftiʿāl form from burning or roasting by fire; its form conveys trying to warm oneself by the fire's heat.
rows.anchor: افتعال من الصلي وهو الشي بالنار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine pronoun in جاءها follows the earlier naming of the light as fire, based on how it appeared to Moses.
rows.anchor: جريا على ما تقدم من تسمية النور نارا بحسب ما لاح لموسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessing or sanctification here captures part of the instruction to remove one's sandals at the sacred valley in 20:12; baraka here means sanctified and purified.
rows.anchor: هو بعض ما اقتضاه قوله في طه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb baraka can be transitive, as in باركك الله, meaning that God made blessing for someone; compare its use at 3:96 and 11:48.
rows.anchor: يستعمل متعديا ، يقال : باركك الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle أن is explanatory after نودي because that verb already implies speech.
rows.anchor: تفسيرية لفعل { نودي } لأن فيه معنى القول دون حروفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reply is set off without a conjunction because that is the convention for dialogue.
rows.anchor: جواب بأسلوب المحاورة فلذلك فصل ولم يعطف كما هي طريقة المحاورات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their نحن represents the kingdom's people capable of war and the officials entrusted with its military decisions.
rows.anchor: من قولهم : نحن ، جماعة المملكة الذين هم من أهل الحرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quwwa includes the means of fighting and prevailing, such as capable fighters and people skilled in war; see 7:145 and 8:60.
rows.anchor: وأطلقت على وسائل القوة كما تقدم في قوله تعالى : وأعدوا لهم ما استطعتم من قوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bas means severity against an enemy; Quranic examples speak of endurance in battle and of enemies' strength among themselves.
rows.anchor: والبأس : الشدة على العدو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They explicitly offer military readiness to defend their kingdom and implicitly signal a preference for force if the queen seeks to compel their submission.
rows.anchor: وهذا الجواب تصريح بأنهم مستعدون للحرب للدفاع عن ملكهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite stating their inclination, they defer to the queen's judgment; the omitted object means command us, and they will obey if she chooses peace.
rows.anchor: ومع إظهار هذا الرأي فوضوا الأمر إلى الملكة لثقتهم بأصالة رأيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb انظري is suspended from governing by the interrogative that follows it, ماذا تأمرين.
rows.anchor: معلق عن العمل بما بعده من الاستفهام وهو { ماذا تأمرين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur previously discussed ماذا at 16:24.
rows.anchor: { ماذا } في قوله : { وإذا قيل لهم ماذا أنزل ربكم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The queen's sentence introduces the decision she is about to announce and provides its rationale.
rows.anchor: مقدمة لما ستلقيه إليهم من عزمها ، ويتضمن تعليلا لما عزمت عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ means accompaniment, and the omitted object of send is a letter and delegation accompanied by a gift, since an envoy would answer Solomon's letter.
rows.anchor: باء المصاحبة . ومفعول { مرسلة } محذوف دل عليه وصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Replying to a letter was an old custom and is treated as Muslim practice and a fellow Muslim's right; Ibn Ashur found no formal ruling in the legal schools.
rows.anchor: وهو من سنن المسلمين ، وعد من حق المسلم على المسلم

rows.speaker: القرطبي
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi says a person who receives a letter with a greeting or similar content should reply, since a letter from an absent person resembles a greeting from someone present.
rows.anchor: قال القرطبي : إذا ورد على إنسان في كتاب بالتحية أو نحوها ينبغي أن يرد الجواب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reportedly considered replying to a letter obligatory, like returning a greeting.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أنه كان يرى رد الكتاب واجبا كرد السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur's apparent view is that a letter containing a greeting requires a written reply including a returned greeting, by analogy with spoken greetings; face-to-face silence more readily causes hostility.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الجواب إن كان عن كتاب مشتمل على صيغة السلام أن يكون رد الجواب واجبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says he found no reply in the Prophet's letters except his response to Musaylima, ending with peace upon whoever follows guidance.
rows.anchor: ولم أر في كتب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم جوابا عن كتاب إلا جوابه عن كتاب مسيلمة والسلام على من اتبع الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadiyya is something offered to draw closeness and affection; hadaya is the standard plural, while the lower Madi dialect says hadawa.
rows.anchor: فالهدية ما يعطى لقصد التقرب والتحبب ، والجمع هدايا على اللغة الفصحى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural hadaya derives from hadaʾi; speakers eased the heavy raised-case yāʾ and shifted the hamza between two alifs to yāʾ, while lower Madi shifts it to wāw.
rows.anchor: وأصل هدايا : هدائي بهمزة بعد ألف الجمع ثم ياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nāẓira is the active participle of نظر meaning to wait or expect.
rows.anchor: اسم فاعل من نظر بمعنى انتظر ، أي مترقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question either explains the queen's waiting or starts a new sentence; the order is changed to show uncertainty about what the envoys will bring back, with bāʾ before its object because interrogative mā takes clause-initial position.
rows.anchor: فغير النظم لما أريد أنها مترددة فيما يرجع به المرسلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who came was the messenger implied by the queen's sending; rasul is grammatically singular but can denote a group, and a caravan could also be the subject because kings' gifts travel in caravans.
rows.anchor: أي فلما جاء الرسول الذي دل عليه قوله : { وإني مرسلة إليهم بهدية }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Solomon refused the gift because the queen had sent it after receiving his letter and apparently left unanswered his demand that they come submitted; he saw it as a bribe to divert his bid for sovereignty over Sheba.
rows.anchor: وقد أبى سليمان قبول الهدية لأن الملكة أرسلتها بعد بلوغ كتابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Solomon addresses the envoys so that his message reaches their queen, since speech to messengers is meant for the sender regarding the purpose of their mission.
rows.anchor: والخطاب في { أتمدونن } لوفد الهدية لقصد تبليغه إلى الملكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is reproachful: the gift and silence about his request imply an attempt to buy him off and assume he needs their money.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام إنكاري لأن حال إرسال الهدية والسكوت عن الجواب يقتضي محاولة صرف سليمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gift appears to have consisted of gold and wealth.
rows.anchor: ويظهر أن الهدية كانت ذهبا ومالا

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read أتمدونني with two nūns.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : { أتمدونني } بنونين

rows.speaker: حمزة وخلف
rows.claim: Hamza and Khalaf read with one doubled nūn through assimilation.
rows.anchor: وقرأه حمزة وخلف بنون واحدة مشددة بالإدغام

words: فَمَآ ءَاتَىٰنِۦَ ٱللَّهُ خَيْرٌۭ مِّمَّآ ءَاتَىٰكُم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa makes the comparison the consequence and reason for his rebuke: God's gifts are better in quality, value, and abundance than theirs.
rows.anchor: والفاء لتفريع الكلام الذي بعدها على الإنكار السابق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanation implies Solomon knew the queen did not know he possessed wealth better than hers; if he thought she knew, the reason would be unnecessary.
rows.anchor: وسوق التعليل يشعر بأنه علم أن الملكة لا تعلم أن لدى سليمان من الأموال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using wāw instead of the actual fa would make the comparison sound circumstantial and suggest that the queen already knew this.
rows.anchor: فلو قال : وما آتاني الله خير مما آتاكم ، لكان مشعرا بأنها تعلم ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bal marks a transition from rebuking their attempt to supply him with money to refusing the gift and sending it back.
rows.anchor: للإضراب الانتقالي وهو انتقال من إنكاره عليهم إمداده بمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The annexation can mean the thing you give as a gift, as an object-like annexation, or the gift brought to you.
rows.anchor: تشبيه ؛ تحتمل أن تكون من إضافة الشيء إلى ما هو في معنى المفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The predicate is an indirect way of indicating that Solomon returns the gift to its giver.
rows.anchor: والخبر استعمل كناية عن رد الهدية للمهدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafraḥūn can mean that they are pleased or that they take pride in the gift: it impresses them, not Solomon, since God gave him better.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون تسرون ، ويجوز أن يكون تفتخرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting أنتُم before the verbal predicate restricts the rejoicing to them, indirectly rejecting their gift.
rows.anchor: وتقديم المسند إليه على الخبر الفعلي في ( أنتم تفرحون ) لإفادة القصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Solomon threatens to send an army the people cannot withstand in battle and to expel them in humiliation.
rows.anchor: وتوعدهم وهددهم بأنه مرسل إليهم جيشا لا قبل لهم بحربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The masculine plural pronouns refer to the people; the expulsion specifically includes those taken captive from the country.
rows.anchor: وضمائر جمع الذكور الغائب في قوله : { فلنأتينهم } و { لنخرجنهم } عائدة إلى القوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jund is the plural of jund, which can also mean a nation, as in the reference to Pharaoh's and Thamud's armies at 85:17–18.
rows.anchor: ويطلق الجند على الأمة قال تعالى { هل أتاك حديث الجنود فرعون وثمود }

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read ونري with the first-person plural of majesty and accusative marking on the verb and Pharaoh with its coordinated nouns.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { ونري } بنون العظمة ونصب الفعل ونصب { فرعون }

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف
rows.claim: Hamza, al-Kisai, and Khalaf read ويرى as a third-person active verb with Pharaoh and its coordinated nouns nominative; the meaning is effectively the same.
rows.anchor: قرأه حمزة والكسائي وخلف { ويرى } بياء الغائب مفتوحة وفتح الراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jund is a collective noun without a singular of the same form: people gathered around one undertaking, as an army serves and obeys its commander.
rows.anchor: هو الجماعة من الناس التي تجتمع على أمر تتبعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about inspiring Moses's mother is linked to the promise to favor the oppressed in 28:5 and details how God would rescue Israel by creating their deliverer.
rows.anchor: عطف على جملة { ونريد أن نمن على الذين استضعفوا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here revelation means inspiration that expands the mother's heart and assures her the thought is divine; truthful inspiration can give righteous people certainty that impels action.
rows.anchor: فإن الإلهام الصادق يعرض للصالحين فيوقع في نفوسهم يقينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inspiration may instead have come through a true dream.
rows.anchor: وقد يكون هذا الوحي برؤيا صادقة رأتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses's mother is unnamed in Jewish books, while the names supplied by commentators are not reliable.
rows.anchor: وأم موسى لم يعرف اسمها في كتب اليهود ، وذكر المفسرون لها أسماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed woman uses Quranic allusion in a short poem; her interlocutor calls her eloquent, glossed here as rhetorically effective.
rows.anchor: وهي تريد التورية بالقرآن . فقال لها : قاتلك الله ما أفصحك يريد ما أبلغك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse compresses two pieces of news, two commands, two prohibitions, and two glad tidings.
rows.anchor: فجمع في آية واحدة خبرين ، وأمرين ، ونهيين ، وبشارتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two reports are the inspiration and the implied foreknowledge that she will fear; the commands are to nurse him and cast him into the river; the prohibitions are not to fear or grieve; the glad tidings are his return and prophethood.
rows.anchor: وقوله { فإذا خفت عليه } لأنه يشعر بأنها ستخاف عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear is expecting something harmful; grief is a state caused by a painful event such as losing or being separated from something beloved.
rows.anchor: والخوف : توقع أمر مكروه ، والحزن : حالة نفسية تنشأ من حادث مكروه للنفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She is told not to fear that the river will kill the child and not to grieve their separation.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : لا تخافي عليه الهلاك من الإلقاء في اليم ، ولا تحزني على فراقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibitions target the causes of fear and grief: anticipating harm and dwelling on the loneliness of separation.
rows.anchor: والنهي عن الخوف وعن الحزن نهي عن سببيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise to return the child explains the two prohibitions by assuring his survival and her reunion; the promise to make him a messenger adds joy.
rows.anchor: وجملة { إنا رادوه إليك } في موقع العلة للنهيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-iltiqāt is the act of picking up something cast on the ground or elsewhere, whether deliberately or inadvertently.
rows.anchor: افتعال من اللقط ، وهو تناول الشيء الملقى في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The act is attributed to Pharaoh's household because one of the women around Pharaoh's daughter retrieved Moses's chest from the Nile, as Exodus chapter 2 relates.
rows.anchor: أسند الالتقاط إلى آل فرعون لأن استخراج تابوت موسى من النهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām is the preposition lām kay, governing a verbal noun understood from أن plus the subjunctive verb and ordinarily marking the agent's motivating cause.
rows.anchor: منسبك من ( أن ) المقدرة بعد اللام ومن الفعل المنصوب بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The family adopted Moses from compassion, not to make him their enemy; because enmity and grief were the outcome, the result is metaphorically phrased as the cause, a dependent metaphor according to most rhetoricians, unlike al-Sakkaki.
rows.anchor: لم يكن داعيهم إلى التقاطه أن يكون لهم عدوا وحزنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to Pharaoh's ruling household as the dynasty, state, or nation; Moses became the enemy of a later Pharaoh and his regime.
rows.anchor: وضمير { لهم } يعود إلى آل فرعون باعتبار الوصف العنواني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥuznan is a verbal noun with an omitted relation meaning grief for them; it is not a source noun used as an adjective for emphasis, and attributing grief to Moses is a causal metaphor.
rows.anchor: ووصفه بالحزن وهو مصدر على تقدير متعلق محذوف ، أي حزنا لهم

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف
rows.claim: Hamza, al-Kisai, and Khalaf read ḥuzn with ḍamma on ḥāʾ and a still zāy; the form is a dialect variant like al-ʿadam and al-ʿudm.
rows.anchor: وقرأه حمزة والكسائي وخلف بضم الحاء وسكون الزاي وهما لغتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their criminality explains God's making Moses their enemy and grief, as punishment for oppressing the Israelites and worshipping idols.
rows.anchor: أي قدر الله نجاة موسى ليكون لهم عدوا وحزنا ، لأنهم كانوا مجرمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khāṭiʾ is the active participle of khaṭiʾa, to commit a sin; its verbal noun is khaṭʾ, distinct from khaṭaʾ, which means unintentional error and comes from أخطأ.
rows.anchor: اسم فاعل من خطىء كفرح إذا فعل الخطيئة وهي الإثم والذنب

rows.speaker: نفطويه والجوهري والحريري
rows.claim: Nuftawayh, followed by al-Jawhari and al-Hariri, distinguishes خطئ for committing sin from أخطأ for making an error, reflecting separate usage by eloquent speakers.
rows.anchor: وعلى التفرقة بين أخطأ وخطىء درج نفطويه وتبعه الجوهري والحريري

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد وابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd and Ibn Qutayba instead treat the two forms as synonyms or dialect variants; al-Zamakhshari's explanation here appears to follow them.
rows.anchor: وذهب أبو عبيد وابن قتيبة إلى أن اللفظين مترادفان وأنهما لغتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses woke afraid of being called to account for killing the Copt and watched what people said, ready to hide or leave if the killing became known; the streets had been empty when it happened.
rows.anchor: أي أصبح خائفا من أن يطالب بدم القبطي الذي قتله وهو يترقب ، أي يراقب ما يقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idhā is suddenative here: Moses was surprised that the man who had sought his help yesterday was seeking it again today.
rows.anchor: و ( إذا ) للمفاجأة ، أي ففاجأه أن الذي استنصره بالأمس يستنصره اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in al-ams replaces a possessive complement: yesterday in relation to that event, not the day before revelation.
rows.anchor: والتعريف في ( الأمس ) عوض عن المضاف إليه ، أي بأمسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istisrākh is an intensive form of shouting or calling for help, equivalent to the earlier istighātha; varying the term provides stylistic diversity.
rows.anchor: والاستصراخ : المبالغة في الصراخ ، أي النداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses's rebuke expresses exasperation that the Israelite's previous call led to a killing; it does not mean Moses will refuse to help, but blames him for repeated disputes.
rows.anchor: وقول موسى له { إنك لغوي مبين } تذمر من الإسرائيلي إذ كان استصراخه السالف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghawi means deeply misguided and poor in judgment: the Israelite provokes someone he cannot handle and asks Moses for help day after day, not that he is unjust or corrupt.
rows.anchor: والغوي : الشديد الغواية وهي الضلال وسوء النظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Batsh means seizing violently; here it refers to striking.
rows.anchor: والبطش : الأخذ بالعنف ، والمراد به الضرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent meaning is that the opponent was a Copt; he may be called enemy to both because his hostility toward the Israelite was public and oppression itself opposed Moses's purified nature.
rows.anchor: وظاهر قوله { عدو لهما } أنه قبطي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is used as a rebuke or denial.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام مستعمل في الإنكار . والجبار : الذي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A jabbar does whatever he wants to harm people and treats them harshly instead of gently; compare the usages at 14:15 and 19:32.
rows.anchor: والجبار : الذي يفعل ما يريد مما يضر بالناس

words: إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَ جَبَّارًۭا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusation is that Moses wants to avenge by force rather than reconcile the disputants.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : إنك تحاول أن تكون متصرفا بالانتقام وبالشدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Copt's words appear to warn Moses against striking him; an exchange followed, then a man came from the far end of the city.
rows.anchor: ويظهر أن كلام القبطي زجر لموسى عن البطش به وصار بينهما حوارا
